summary: Add a nullable marketing_opt_in column with default False, backfill all existing rows to False, deploy the new version with state_only migration, retire the old version, then alter the column to NOT NULL. The column’s DB default False ensures old‑version inserts also receive False, preventing NULLs during the overlap.
write_consistency: The column is created with DEFAULT FALSE, so any INSERT from the old version (which does not know the column) receives False instead of NULL. A backfill UPDATE sets every existing row to False before the new version starts. After retire_old only the new version writes, and its code always includes the column, guaranteeing no NULLs remain when the column is finally set NOT NULL.

stages.description: Add nullable boolean column marketing_opt_in with default False.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN marketing_opt_in BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE;

stages.description: Set marketing_opt_in to False for all rows (including those that were NULL after column addition).
Retire the old Saleor version; after this only the new version handles traffic.
Make marketing_opt_in NOT NULL; succeeds because all rows are already False.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ALTER COLUMN marketing_opt_in SET NOT NULL;
